tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (job fails, hangs, denied access, etc.) rather than internal implementation, and explicitly lists many trigger contexts (S3/KMS/IAM denial, InsufficientInstanceCapacity, OOM, spot interruption, VPC timeout, empty channels, hidden metrics, warm pool, billed GPU time) even covering cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly ('even if they do not mention execution roles, key policies...'). It is a dense but single, cohesive paragraph appropriate for the scope of the skill.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a training job is denied access to S3, a KMS key or iam:PassRole, fails with InsufficientInstanceCapacity, ResourceLimitExceeded or out of memory, goes to Failed with no logs...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body stays domain-specific throughout, covering SageMaker-specific checks, error patterns, and procedures without explaining general concepts the agent already knows (e.g., what training jobs or S3 are).
tests.evidence: Grounded in the LLM-SM check family under checks-sagemaker-training.md — the LLM-SM-TRAIN-* sub-family for training / customization

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The check catalog table and router table are compact index/summary tables (what-it-catches, first-read pointers) rather than full detailed reference content; the detailed material is explicitly deferred to references/ files.
tests.evidence: The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference — the table below is a what-it-catches index.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown links in the body (checks-sagemaker-training.md, collection-reference.md, api-quirks.md, known-causes.md, metrics-and-logs.md).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Reference links consistently specify when to load, e.g. tied to symptoms or steps.
tests.evidence: Load [known-causes.md](references/known-causes.md) whenever the user names an error or symptom; match it to a section, check the cited AWS page, and give the cause, how to confirm it, and the fix.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference paths use relative paths from the skill root in the format references/<file>.md.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: The skill is prescriptive for fragile diagnostic classification (exact check-id matching, pending-vs-failed distinction) while giving reasoning/why explanations for judgment calls, appropriately matching rigor to fragility.
tests.evidence: The capacity-vs-quota split is opposite remediations — read both the FailureReason and the quota value (api-quirks.md §2).

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The router and check tables designate a clear 'First read' / default API call per symptom rather than listing multiple equal options.
tests.evidence: | My training job failed, the data looks corrupt or won't parse | `DescribeTrainingJob` `FailureReason`, then the JSONL sample |

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure and Router teach a generalizable diagnostic approach (classify, confirm, report) applicable to any training job, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Classify Pending-vs-Failed... If Failed, bucket the FailureReason into exactly one cause and cite the check

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has explicit 'Common wrong answers' and 'Error Handling' sections documenting non-obvious API quirks and traps.
tests.evidence: "The job is InProgress with Pending, so it is failing." A job waiting on GPU capacity is control-plane-healthy, not Failed.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: A health report template is provided in assets/ and referenced for use when a full report is requested.
tests.evidence: Use [training-job-health-report-template.md](assets/training-job-health-report-template.md) when a full report is requested.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large output template is embedded inline in the body; the template lives in assets/ and is referenced conditionally.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is linked in the body.
tests.evidence: [training-job-health-report-template.md](assets/training-job-health-report-template.md) — load when a full report is requested

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies when to load it (full report requested).
tests.evidence: load when a full report is requested: training/customization report format (per-job state, failure classification, findings, cost note, disclosed scope).

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure, which is the ordered dependent workflow, uses checkbox checklist format with Step N labeling.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill has an explicit 'Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' section instructing the agent to check its own findings before presenting.
tests.evidence: Before presenting, re-check your output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion.
